The theorem claims  

\[
\text{Nat.maxPowDiv } 2 \Bigl(\prod_{i=1}^{9} i!\Bigr) = 30 .
\]

In Mathlib, `Nat.maxPowDiv p n` is defined as the *largest power of* `p` that divides `n`, i.e.

\[
\text{Nat.maxPowDiv } p n = p^{\text{Nat.multiplicity } p n}.
\]

Hence the value of `Nat.maxPowDiv 2 …` must be a power of 2.  
The product \(\prod_{i=1}^{9} i!\) has a 2‑adic valuation

\[
\sum_{i=1}^{9} v_2(i!) = 0+1+1+3+3+4+4+7+7 = 30,
\]

so  

\[
\text{Nat.multiplicity } 2 \Bigl(\prod_{i=1}^{9} i!\Bigr)=30,
\qquad
\text{Nat.maxPowDiv } 2 \Bigl(\prod_{i=1}^{9} i!\Bigr)=2^{30}.
\]

Therefore the right‑hand side of the statement should be `2 ^ 30`, not `30`.  
Alternatively, if the intended quantity is the exponent, the statement should use `Nat.multiplicity 2 … = 30`.

Because the asserted equality contradicts the definition of `Nat.maxPowDiv`, the theorem is mathematically false as written.
